小兒
小兒病難治

治之之難，難以故人。古人莫醫一小兒益，小兒一問謹難，家醫十丈夫莫醫小兒，雞人難謹，寧醫家，幼經活，盛難不經終，能切，聲不能擊。

為治之，九難以如故，也藏府之虛，皮骨弱，大方脈為難，氣未盛，活經幼難終。

言其病源，盖療之，者其陰陽，表裏，莫易知，非親，形察，色聽，聲不能切。

如手經，不能指，疾痛易之，亦難，知皮骨，冷易弱，血氣未，為脈難。

究而先生，之夫，又月，有三孕，而右腎，二月，之胎，為男陰包，桃陽花。

臟腑生成

由肝生，也肝生，胃為陰，脾則為，心以小，其它陰，已也，者次，大水生，五胆生，陽。

膽生胃，其膜，生心，以小腸，生三焦，以生其，膜已，者小膽。
translation:
Dongui Bogam, Miscellaneous Diseases, Volume 11

Composed by royal physician Heo Jun, holder of the rank of Chunggeun Jeongnyang Hosung, meritorious subject, Senior First Rank, Lord of Yangpyeong, by royal command.

Pediatrics (Children's Diseases)
On the Difficulty of Treating Children's Diseases

It is said: treating children's diseases is the most difficult of all. Ancient physicians said they would rather treat ten adult men than one child. The reason is that children cannot answer questions, making diagnosis extremely difficult. Even experienced family physicians find it hard: children cannot describe their symptoms, cannot communicate their pain, and it is impossible to rely on verbal inquiry.

In treating children, the nine difficulties arise because: the organs and viscera are vacuous and weak, the bones and flesh are delicate, and the methods used for adult medicine are difficult to apply; the vital energies are not yet fully developed, making treatment of young children especially challenging.

When speaking of the source of illness, treatment is complicated because in children the distinction between yin and yang, interior and exterior, is not easily known. Without direct observation — examining the complexion and listening to sounds — it is impossible to assess the pulse.

One cannot rely on palpation of the channels with the hand; pain is hard to pinpoint; the skin and bones are cold and soft; the blood and qi are undeveloped, making pulse diagnosis extremely difficult.

Investigating the formation of the organs: it begins with the liver; the gallbladder forms the stomach; the membrane generates the heart; the small intestine gives rise to the triple burner; from these the membranes are produced; the lesser gallbladder is formed last.

On the Formation of the Viscera and Organs

The liver generates; the gallbladder generates the stomach; its membranes generate the heart; the small intestine generates the triple burner; from these the membranes are completed; the lesser gallbladder is the last.

translation:
Methods for Detoxifying the Newborn

Simmer the juice; when it froths, do not discard it. Stop once it reaches the mouth. While the infant is still in the womb, the mouth contains foul matter. Wrap a finger in soft silk cloth and wipe the foul matter from inside the infant's mouth. When the child is born and does not cry, use licorice root (gancao) brewed fresh; after birth, boil it more concentrated and give it once.

Methods for Bathing the Newborn

Use licorice root decocted; in the morning, use a large piece of soft cloth wrapped around the infant; use it from the buttocks inward; it is said to wrap the infant's bladder and urine area, binding it around; then feed breast milk, the yellow colostrum first, measuring the amount accordingly.

[Right-side column — anatomical enumeration text:]
The intestines have two layers; the channels pass through fire; six bowels arise from this, forming two yang [channels]; their ten-fold branching forms two or three of the Triple Burner channels; one generation of vessels; eighteen vessels; ten visceral channels; three generations; ten thousand; four hundred; six hundred; one thousand nodes of bone; collateral channels; bone nodes; collaterals; three-three generations; one hundred; ten thousand; four; ten; grandchild-collaterals; ten; five major channels; born.

[Continuing enumeration of acupuncture points, vessels, and bone nodes referring to classical channel theory totals of 365 collaterals, thousands of bone segments, and the standard counts of primary and secondary channels.]

One must not neglect caution in these matters. When bathing the newborn in warm water, one must not let the child become startled. Examine the skull carefully. When shaving and washing, use a small amount of ox bile decocted appropriately for the infant.

translation:
Methods for Cutting the Umbilical Cord at Birth

The placental cord connects the child in the womb to the mother's umbilical cord. For ten months, through the navel, the child and mother share breath and vital energy. After the cord is cut, even though the infant has been born from the womb, one must use soft cloth to wrap and cover the navel stump. When a newborn's navel stump is to be treated, use soft silk to gently rub and massage it by hand until it becomes soft. Gently rub and massage it; if it remains hard, apply soft cloth over the navel stump and cover it.

When the cord area is firm, remove the residual blood by waiting; the cord will dry and the flow will cease. Use a soft band to gently twist and rub it. If there is swelling or hardness that does not disperse, gently soften it, then apply moxa around the navel.

Watch the root of the cord and wait for it to fall off naturally after two to three days. Many practitioners wait until the navel stump falls, then apply moxa around the four sides of the infant's navel area.

Naturally the juice or fluid within will dry up; one may use fragrant oil to fumigate it. The belly area should be kept free of separation. Apply moxa to the navel stump area.

Only then, after some time, if disease or stagnation appears, or wind-cold attacks, one may wash and bathe. If the navel stump has not yet been cut properly, do not forcibly cut it.

Methods for Selecting a Wet Nurse

The wet nurse must be in good physical and mental health before she can serve. Afterward, she may bathe. She must not be afflicted with any strong illness.

She should circulate warmth and avoid cold; she should be able to eat easily and not go hungry. Her disposition should be harmonious and regulated, her temperament calm, her diet balanced. She should eat meat in moderation to maintain adequate nourishment and healthy weight.

She must not have chronic diseases, and should avoid greasy or rich foods such as chicken.

She should not suffer from epilepsy or similar convulsive conditions. Her diet should avoid sour, fatty, or excessively rich foods.

She should not engage in sexual intercourse, and must avoid sour, irritating, fatty, or rich foods.

Whatever she eats and drinks passes into the breast milk, which the infant drinks. This directly affects the infant's digestion and overall constitution, and so the wet nurse must regulate her diet and daily habits accordingly.

translation:
Breast Milk and Infant Feeding Methods (小兒乳哺法):

Breast milk must not be given carelessly. One should be cautious: if the milk causes the child to become ill or suffer from accumulated stagnation, one must consult and adjust the diet and feeding accordingly, so that the mother and child are both at peace.

The first milk after birth, if it causes the child illness, one must seek guidance, and adjust the food and drink accordingly, choosing appropriate treatments so the child remains safe.

The nature of breast milk changes according to the mother's character, temperament, constitution, and emotional disposition. If the mother's temperament is urgent or agitated, this affects the bones and constitution of the child.

Regarding the method of nursing infants: Breast milk should not be given carelessly or without attentiveness. Up to six years of age, before the child grows large, sufficient blood must be established. After nursing, nourishment should be continued appropriately each day.

One should not allow the child to drink without regulation; otherwise the milk will stagnate in the stomach, making it difficult to digest, and the child may vomit.

After nursing, food should not immediately be given, as this causes the milk to stagnate in the stomach, making it hard to expel by vomiting.

If milk and food accumulate in the abdomen, it causes pain from stagnant qi and blood, and generates heat. Such stagnation is difficult to transform. One should avoid giving raw chestnuts and other such foods externally.

When the stomach is still delicate and narrow, blood and qi pain with fever and illness that is difficult to resolve should be managed through proper nourishment. Avoid steamed and raw chestnuts and similar flavors.

Dried persimmons and their hot, crisp nature — infants whose skin and flesh are still tender should not be exposed too early to warmth, as the yang energy enters the skin layers easily.

Methods for Protecting Children (小兒保護法):

translation:
Ten Methods for Raising Children

First: Keep the back warm. Second: Keep the abdomen warm. Third: Keep the feet warm. Fourth: Keep the head cool. Fifth: Keep the chest and heart cool. Sixth: Do not let the child see strange or frightening things. Seventh: Do not let the child cry excessively. Eighth: Do not administer calomel (light powder) or cinnabar. Ninth: Do not let the child sleep on damp ground. Tenth: Do not bathe the child too frequently.

When the weather brings illness, warmth helps; support the small child — in daytime let them be exposed to air so the blood and qi become strong and firm, so that the sinews and bones are well-formed.

[The following sections discuss keeping the child's sides and pillow warm, covering with clothing at the right times, using cotton padding when cold, positioning the child's head and face, and protecting the infant's bones.]

[Sections on clothing discuss using old softened garments as they are gentle on the infant's sinews and bones, how new garments should be made in the child's shape so that the true qi is nourished and the child gains longevity; old cloth retains gentle energy that nurtures the infant, and new silk gauze garments should not be used too early as they may harm the child.]

[On feeding: do not bring the child out before six months; in the first months use only simple wrappings.]

Song of Nurturing and Care:
Regarding milk — at seven months nourish the child's spleen and stomach; do not administer calomel or cinnabar; at ten months reduce fluid intake; throughout, nurture the child properly.

For children: one must protect and adjust the spleen; being covered appropriately in single or layered garments as the season requires; gently rub and settle the stomach; avoid inappropriate foods.

變蒸候

風順見時日寒俗謂之牙生骨長比如蠶之有眠龍○

暑者頻見時日寒俗謂之小兒變蒸虎胎毒心也咄此類變生而長也陰陽七水情火蒸○

小兒變蒸者由小血氣而蒸形體之成就也是咄○三十二日變者生二藏陰陽七情火蒸○

蘇小兒由血氣而變蒸形體之成就也是前日何至三十藏之變者生二氣陰陽七情火蒸○

單即由變蒸生也也情蓋有兒異生蘇之前骨脈分精神人有經總三藏府一意變每故變之○

何以謂三象天十情有兒以長期骨脈體精神人有經總三百六十五藏初意智故變之蒸○

骨九三以天十歲以分十二人有經三百六十五藏初意智故每變之蒸生膀胱○

蒸腸十十六二一日變生心骨一六十四十日愛二生蒸膀胱生○

百日三八二四蒸膽二五大五二胃八生肺九二十四二愛百二十五日十六愛少陽○

大焦合公云乃成八人四肢長碎齒變生於五十徵也蒸乃是蒸者蒸養癆地之○
translation:
On the Symptoms of Bian Zheng (Developmental Changes and Steaming Fever in Infants)

What is commonly called "teething and bone growth" is like the silkworm entering its dormant phase. (Dragon symbol)

In hot seasons, when the weather turns cold, it is popularly called the infant's "bian zheng" (developmental transformation). This is related to the poison from the tiger fetal stage, and pertains to the heart. These transformations belong to the same category of developmental growth. The yin-yang and seven emotions give rise to steaming fever.

Small children undergo "bian zheng" (developmental transformation and steaming) because their blood and qi are still forming their bodies and physical constitution. This is why at thirty-two days there is a transformation corresponding to two viscera, governed by yin-yang and the seven emotions.

The infant's bian zheng arises from blood and qi transforming and steaming to complete the formation of the body. Each stage corresponds to the growth of the viscera, yin-yang, and the seven emotions.

The transformations arise directly from the steaming process. The child's unusual growth periods correspond to the bones, vessels, essence, spirit, and the meridians which total three hundred sixty-five visceral systems. Each transformation has its own meaning and the steaming corresponds to the bladder.

Every thirty-two days there is a transformation. The body's meridians number three hundred sixty-five, corresponding to the viscera. Intelligence and will develop with each transformation, with the steaming corresponding to the bladder.

At ninety-six days there is a transformation corresponding to the small intestine and heart. At one hundred sixty days, another transformation occurs corresponding to the bladder.

At one hundred days the small steaming occurs. At one hundred ten days, transformations correspond to the gallbladder and liver. At one hundred ninety days, transformations correspond to the bladder.

At three hundred days, transformations correspond to the gallbladder. At three hundred eighty days, transformations correspond to the stomach. At various intervals, transformations correspond to the lungs, pericardium, and lesser yang meridian.

The Triple Burner and gallbladder undergo transformations at various stages. The stomach, hands, and pericardium complete their transformations by two hundred fifty days, corresponding to the lesser yang.

When there is no fixed form and no speech, after the initial stage, if the child cannot yet speak or show joy, this is related to the lesser yang heavenly cycle.

The great heat combining with the child's development means the child grows limbs, teeth emerge, and the body fully develops by fifty units of transformation. This is the true meaning of the steaming nurturing process.

translation:
Childhood Recurring Seizure Disorders and Nightmare Disorders

In cases of grand府pattern: there may be mild sweating or mild fever with irritability. In vomiting, one should use Rabbit Powder (兔散) for conditions resembling fish-type epilepsy (魚癇). When mild, the steaming fever resolves in five days; when severe, it resolves in seven or eight days, with the heat clearing from the center outward. For more severe cases, use Purple Frost Pill (紫霜丸) to clear the exterior.

To prevent it: if the condition resembles fish-type epilepsy, when mild it resolves in five days; when severe in seven or eight days. One may safely administer medicines for epilepsy, and also use moxibustion and acupuncture needles for cure. For heat patterns, use harmonizing and balancing methods.

Upon hearing: for infant worm disorders, divide into five parts. For the four worm types, have the child use fragrant herbs, roast and grind the ash finely, and use with millet gruel.

For conditions of the body: use this formula to expel worms. After moxibustion, have the child heat-roast and grind the ash with the medicine together.

For fever with verification: use Alfalfa roasted preparation. In such worm-epilepsy disorders, first apply moxibustion, then have the child roast and chew the ash medicine.

Guide through the abdomen pattern with Rong-Ji-Jin formula. In the small treatise: childhood worm disorders are a type of epilepsy. The child becomes sallow and thin but can still walk; grind the medicine finely.

For those with mild discomfort and diarrhea with cold, it is appropriate to take Dragon Fur Percolating Decoction (龍毛滲湯). The Heron-type disorder is also called childhood ghost-return (小鬼歸). Its symptoms are spiritual in nature; the child stands but the bones may also be affected.

Dragon Gallbladder Decoction (Longdan Tang)

Ingredients: One preparation consists of: raw/roasted rhubarb (2 qian), Chinese gentian (Longdan), bupleurum (Chaihu), scutellaria root (Huangqin), platycodon root (Jiegeng), uncaria vine (Gouteng), and tangerine peel. Take two doses on the right side as directed.

Method for Determining a Child's Longevity at Birth

At the time of birth, there are signs that indicate whether the child will live long or die young. In general, one can tell by observing the infant at the time of birth. After ten years of age, one can know further. By observing the child's breathing and vital energy from a young age, one can predict longevity.

Children who are born with a strong cry, vigorous movements, and good responsiveness, who return to normal quickly, who are alert and lively — these children tend toward long life.

Children born without proper brain development, with pale and bloodless complexion, with a soft and weak body, who sweat easily and lack vigor, who are small and slow — these tend toward short life.

Further signs: if the child has good vision and proper comportment, with strong bones, good teeth erupting early, and normal development milestones — these are signs of longevity.

If the child is irritable, with poor constitution inherited from parents, and reaches developmental milestones late — this is a sign of shortened life.

If the child cannot walk, cannot stand, cannot speak at the appropriate ages, or has bones that fail to develop properly — these are signs of death.

A child born with no scrotum, or with white discoloration below, or who cannot recover and rise — these are signs of early death.

translation:
On Sounds: Light and Heavy, Hoarse and Wet/Dry

[Concerning types of sounds in illness:] A heavy sound indicates fright; a light sound indicates weakness. Wind-sounds indicate wind-cold; sounds of qi indicate qi disorders. A sunken, quiet sound is serious. When sounds arise with pox or fright, one must observe them carefully. If the voice is lost suddenly, this is critical. A voice that breaks off and does not continue indicates a blocked condition. Various signs relating to sounds and their clinical significance are to be found in the detailed discussion.

Emergency Conditions of the Newborn Child

[Including:] Lockjaw (噤口), Pursed Mouth (撮口), and Umbilical Wind (臍風)

All [of these conditions] arise because toxic heat accumulated in the womb sinks into the heart; the eyes cannot open, there is a hoarse cry, and white foam is discharged from the mouth. In the early days after birth, if the infant has white eyebrows [and related signs], the condition is called "Chicken Mouth" [a form of neonatal tetanus]. One applies [treatment] to the outside of the nose and mouth area.

[Treatment:] Use ground [medicinals] and juice preparations. Rub with the finger. Use cinnabar (辰砂) and well-flower water (井花水) — this is the most effective method. Also: earthworm (地龍), Notopterygium (羌), and other [herbs], decocted and applied by rubbing. See the detailed prescriptions below.

When the nine throat conditions show bluish-black discoloration at the edges, blackening of the fingernails, or death-rot visible inside — these are fatal signs. 治口風及切胞風膈風蝎梢四十九枚炒以薄荷葉卷細木調綠礬勻四十九蒿以碙砂內滾計

translation:
Scorpion Tail Powder
Treats oral wind, cuts membrane wind, diaphragm wind. Take 49 pieces of scorpion tails, dry-fry them, roll them in mint leaves, grind finely into powder, mix with green vitriol evenly; 49 pieces [processed] with borax internally dissolved.

Dry-fry, each time use fresh or dried mint leaves, a small amount. Grind the right ingredients into fine powder, mix evenly with purple realgar [preparation].

Dispelling Wind Powder
Take half a unit [dose]; treats all types of wind syndrome where the patient cries much, with white discharge from the mouth — take the whole amount of full scorpions, twenty-one units, mixed two doses each time of ten.

Regulate Qi and Benefit the Yellow Powder
Use half a unit of poppy [preparation], decocted; treats [conditions involving] gold and silver [minerals], regulates the diaphragm. White-headed, red-footed scorpions, stir-fried.
Apply without moxibustion on scorpion tail wind, four to three conditions, white [ingredient], literary bone, nasal interior, treasure, stir-fried.
Each time guard with a sickle-shaped tool to adjust, one unit dose taken with Sichuan [herb] decoction.

Golden Crow Powder
With poppy, five treatments for generalized wind, named Xiāng; red, permitted, with pine powder, in wine, half soaked; use moxibustion with Golden Crow [preparation].
Agastache, wheat, with light and measured portions; each time use thin [decoction], one unit, decocted in broth, adjusted to one unit dose, with moxibustion.

Penetrating the Heart Drink
Decoct scallion in broth. Adjust and take with the named preparation. Clear heart fire, promote urination, relieve convulsions: Akebia stem, red poria, apricot kernel, scutellaria root, licorice — 4 fen each. Decoct on the right [side of the method].

translation:
Gwal Maek San (Scraping Membrane Powder)
Take one dose. Add rush pith [lamp wick herb].
Whirling at the temples, hence named
Green onion eyes [a type of eye condition].
The eye protrudes, the heart spins.
Swelling spreads, cannot dry out.
Dried, or mix with oil and apply.
Use soot from the bottom of a pot.

Five-Penetrating Ointment (O Tong Go)
Treats sudden swelling.
Fever, wind, hold equally divided [in equal parts].
Fresh rehmannia,
Four [ingredients] of fresh trichosanthes,
Apply in a ring.
Grind white trichosanthes root with dangui [Angelica sinensis],
Seed of a field [herb].
Apply repeatedly.

[Continuation of application instructions:]
Heals and drains while
Treating uniformly.
Flesh [affected area], apply the formula together,
Wrap and cover the membrane, fresh rehmannia on top,
Four fresh trichosanthes, ring-shaped application,
Grind white trichosanthes with dangui and seed,
Apply repeatedly.

Fragrant Snail Ointment (Hyang Ra Go)
Apply by rubbing onto the swelling, which is hard like a plate.
For children, the spirit [qi] must be replenished.
Reapply snail [preparation] three times.
Pain ceases, the swelling dissipates.
Use a small amount.

Fright Disorders and Sudden Malignant Qi (Yongoh Jungang)
When suddenly afflicted, [the patient shows] wide-eyed stiffness,
The face changes color, the knees ache,
The mouth pulls to one side, phlegm rises,
Vomiting, bluish-yellow-white discoloration [of complexion].
Some [cases are treated] as in Buddhist temple [tradition],
Where divine substances or water are used,
Or [remedies] are not combined with other ingredients.

Fresh [treatment]: even though [one presses the] ear,
Using the fingernail, [find] the point of color change,
Left or right side of the mouth contracts,
Bluish, yellow, or white [discoloration],
Small blisters or bony prominences appear,
Roast [the herb] until it smokes,
Fumigate the abdomen.

[Then:] Pierce the ear
With the middle fingernail, stimulate the point,
Mix with vinegar, simmer into a small poultice,
Roast and fumigate with smoke,
Then take orally.
Use Fragrant Su He Yuan [a prepared pill],
Ground to powder, to revive [the patient],
Mix with vinegar, simmer,
Wrap in a small bundle, roast until smoking,
Fumigate and administer.

Soap thorn [Gleditsia] and realgar powder,
Blow into the nose.
No one dies [from this condition if treated].
Use Bi Xie [to repel evil qi],
For bluish-black [complexion], revive immediately,
Use Su He Yuan [storax pill] dissolved in warm water,
This type of preparation
Combined with combined fragrant pills,
One qian [unit of weight] each.

研和醋一合服之即差○客忤取五政三合水濕以摩差

為中馬心汗及氣上或下子大馬久鷺中兒忤自取有上及足路心各五六之面以摩差

雄廬散治兒客忤即愈身每一字雄黃一錢乳香五分麝香一字以勻右為衣覆

辟邪黃土膏治小兒鬼祟惡氣降塵填香各五白錢右香五沉香末八尾頭骨黃玉人

小兒日夜啼令有四中腹一又面三日而寒常二日口熟白三日口有癥氣重手舌

湯錢香化下參治兒一口錢煉羽中又令和兒勻膝帶作又燒取少內許尤以妙藏香香

translation:
Grind and mix with vinegar, one he (unit of volume), take orally; the condition will immediately improve. For a child suffering from fright from a stranger (keogeo), take five portions of three items, mix with water, and rub on the affected area to cure.

Hungsno Powder (Xionglu San): Treats infantile fright from strangers (keogeo). Apply immediately to the body. Each dose: one pun of realgar (xionghuang), one qian of frankincense (ruxiang), five fen of musk (shexiang), and one pun. Mix evenly. The right side serves as a cover.

Bixa Huangtu Ointment (to ward off evil): Treats children suffering from ghost-induced ailments and malign qi. Descend the dust and fill with incense, five portions each, white coins; right side: five portions of incense, sinking fragrance powder, eight tails, head bone, yellow jade.

Night Crying: When yin energy in the feet is excessive and cold, pain occurs in the morning; after midnight it worsens and then subsides. It is appropriate to use the Six Spirits Decoction (Liushen Yi), dose by the cup at night.

Infantile day and night crying: There are four types. First, cold in the abdomen. Second, after some days, the face and body become feverish. Third, the mouth shows symptoms of accumulation. Fourth, excessive qi and heaviness of tongue.

Decoction: Take one qian of ginseng, dissolve; treat the child with one portion, one qian of refined [ingredients]. Mix evenly, apply to the knee area as a compress; burn and take a small amount internally; also use fragrant herbs.

Hungsno Powder composition: Treats children; grind finely, dissolve in water, adjust the spirit-calming heart formula; apply to the child's head, yellow earth as base, carve and fill each in equal portions.

translation:
Pig's Milk Paste
Treats night crying in infants. Ingredients: cinnabar (zhusha), jade, saposhnikovia root (fangfeng), one qian each. Mix cinnabar with cow's milk to make a thin dew-like preparation, place in mouth, let the child swallow it.

Fright-Calming Powder
Treats fright in infants. Finely grind ingredients, mix cinnabar with cow's milk into a thin preparation, place in mouth. Apply to dry mouth with a rush-pith wick at night. Use two to four rush-pith lamp flower beads, grind finely, mix with honey. An alternate formula uses rush-pith heart.

Rush-Pith Heart Powder
Treats heart and upper diaphragm conditions in children, calms the heart and stops symptoms temporarily at night. Uses cinnabar, mother's milk, lamp flower beads, two portions, refine finely with honey, four days of grinding, using rush-pith heart.

Coptis Drink
Take the juice, treats heart conditions using licorice, moxa at the heart region, stops sudden heat at night. Take ginger with ten portions of ginseng, two qian, one slice of fresh ginger, cut, decoct in water with licorice.

Cicada Flower Powder
Treats newborn infant night crying. Use one zi (small measure) of powdered cicada combined with mint, to drive away evil influences. Mix with half a portion of wine, powder it, or stop immediately.

Five Organs' Deficiency and Excess Patterns
For early life and treatment of infants, use one word's worth of powdered mint, as if driving away evil, add a little wine, mix and swallow half a portion powdered. If the condition is excess, do not supplement; if deficient, supplement. When reaching the organ, administer rescue treatment. If the position cannot be filled, the remainder applies to organ disease until spring, when supplementation reaches the organ.

Five Organs' Deficiency and Excess Patterns: The daughter organ must first be replenished at its root position. If excess, drain the child organ; if deficient, supplement. Use this method to regulate yang and restore balance, with a little mixed and swallowed, stopping immediately.

translation:
Heart governs fright

When excess: the child cries with a sharp voice, develops fever, drinks water, and has convulsions; there is upward flushing. When the Heart is deficient and hot, the face is flushed.

When ill: the qi is excessive and forceful, causing cries and loss of speech. When excess, one can obtain free flow, the hands move, there is a tendency to look upward and have convulsions.

The tongue should be cooled; use cooling and bridging [herbs]. When deficient, unable to generate [adequate qi], crying is difficult, convulsions arise with fever.

Use cooling decoctions for the Heart; the mind is unsettled, eyes are red, dispersing [herbs are indicated]. Guard against seeing fusions; combine with drinks.

The Heart governs heat; when combined with vexation and heat on the face and above.

Liver governs wind

Excess: the hands draw in, clothes are not changed, gaze turns, large pupils, red complexion, dispersing [herbs], guard against seeing fusions.

Deficiency: yawning, gaping, objects appear to spin, days pass, fright convulsions occur with sudden cries.

When deficient, convulsions arise with arching of the back; use Rehmannia [Dihuang] decoction.

Spleen governs weakness

When excess: illness with convulsions, the body becomes stiff with arching back; use Dihuang Qing Yuan [formula].

When deficient: fever, excessive sleep, drinking of water, eating and drinking are affected. Excess: somnolence, heavy body, drowsiness without thirst. Deficient: drinks water.

Heat diarrhea arises; red, white, and yellow colored diarrhea, or abdominal masses and movement; use appropriate [formulas]. For white-colored diarrhea, use [the indicated formula].

text:
肺主喘

氣白長主氣顴短。
後用阿膠散。若不則唇白色長出而氣少氣。先肺病益補黃蠟。

門摳子故都也主之膠之虛。不能相當。兩久則氣便日壓而此唇以白唇診者肺之法母也。

藏唇法白也色者質虛。○肺不能兩顴廉。肺微弦則唇白色長出而氣少先肺病益補肺散。當治肺虛也。

腎主虛

小中白過八晴之顴兒。○本骨病疾由無精氣光不盛則體骨神氣重。○足腎虛。

因骨重難而不白也頻數解開面色奄能白者。不又及也腎不足乃則盛而難乏養或難長。日虛。有盖腎下則寒盖有長。

明病皆宜補腎致到整腎非細也頻也。○又也腎不足虛者自寒自腎主珉惟腎珉無實。○但腎主兒脊自寒。

下珍寬足熟下寬是者腎重難欲墜心火而臨身也。腎足熟者。

病則足黑經寒則是腎兩六味地黃主之藏惟腎珉無實。○小兒脊自
translation:
The Lung Governs Panting (Dyspnea)

When the qi is deficient, the complexion appears pale, the breathing becomes short. Afterward use Agiao (Donkey-hide gelatin) Powder. If the lips turn white and the color becomes prolonged, and the qi output is reduced and sparse, first treat the lung disease by supplementing and nourishing with Yellow Wax formula.

When the lung qi is unable to properly distribute, and the cheekbones show signs of abnormality, the lung becomes weak and thin. If the lips are white and breathing is prolonged with reduced qi, first treat the lung disease by supplementing and nourishing the lung with the Dispersing Powder. This is the method for treating lung deficiency.

The Kidney Governs Deficiency

When the bones are heavy and the eyes appear sunken, and the fontanelle is affected — this indicates essence and qi are not flourishing, resulting in heavy bones and depressed spirit-qi, and overall kidney deficiency.

When the bones are heavy and one cannot easily rise, the complexion is not bright, the kidney is insufficient, making it difficult to nourish and grow over time, leading to chronic deficiency.

All such cases should be treated by supplementing the kidney. The kidney governs the marrow; when kidney marrow is depleted there is no substantial reserve. In young children, the spine feels cold, indicating self-cold arising from kidney deficiency.

Symptoms include heaviness in the lower body, a sensation of downward prolapse, heart-fire flaring upward, with the body feeling heavy. When kidney heat reaches the feet, these symptoms occur.

When the feet turn dark and cold, this belongs to the kidney pattern. The Six-Ingredient Rehmannia Pill (Liuwei Dihuang) governs this condition. The kidney marrow being depleted means there is no surplus. In young children, the spine feeling cold from within is also a sign.

五臟相乘

導者赤不散青腎覆衣也。心氣寬熱則上元宜乘夫邪為微大邪。母為肝藏靈相乘實。藏邪乘後車勝之。肝藏靈實邪者從前來勝者為微邪。從後來者為賊邪。從所生來者為虛邪。從所勝來者為實邪。自病者為正邪。凡五藏病必先治補者乘邪。從前來勝者為微邪。從後來者為賊邪。

而乘莫莫為調之後○乘藏肝病此必○子于下虛者為正邪○備乘○妻母為乘。夫邪為微大邪。乘實相藏靈。乘後車勝之者。從前來勝苦見微邪靜雷之○如好勝者從後實實為邪。乘相藏靈。大乘。

病門從後○從者藏所為虛邪○停不者為賊邪。從所來勝者為微邪。萬東又見苦詳靜雷邪。乘實相藏靈。乘後車勝之。

戊則伏疾癢脾○火火動則墮滯則為癇疾或火咬則為急驚或慢驚或風來或去慢風疾為慢驚純用醋藥為酷驚藥。

當則為養滿血青火皆由使肥濕則為古濕而成癇則以為鈎疾或為火咬則為急驚或慢驚去慢風。

義以小方也當為養滿血藥為使古方湯以加白芍為尽純用醋藥鈎疾。

鷺風證

趙發風則之證驚有怠驚也慢驚以其兒之病怠急慢證死須夫故疾也等之○景小兒者最為驚風疾，小兒急者三者之異鷺無鷺
translation:
The Five Viscera Overcoming One Another

When one organ overcomes another, the pathogenic influences can be classified as follows: When the evil comes from the organ that one overcomes (the "conquered" direction), it is called a "slight evil." When it comes from behind (the organ that overcomes it), it is called a "robber evil." When it comes from the organ that generated it (its mother organ), it is called a "deficiency evil." When it comes from the organ it generates (its child organ), it is called an "excess evil." When the illness arises within the organ itself, it is called a "correct evil." In all five visceral diseases, one must first treat by supplementing, and address the pathogenic evil accordingly.

The liver stores the ethereal soul; excess in the liver is associated with robber evil coming from behind. Coming from the front and overcoming is a slight evil. The subtle signs of slight evil appear calm at first. Whatever overcomes from behind produces an excess condition. These relationships govern the mutual overcoming among the viscera.

Regarding stagnation: When fire stirs, there is heaviness and sluggishness, which can produce convulsive disorders. If fire attacks, there may be acute fright convulsions or slow fright convulsions. When wind comes and goes, it produces slow wind patterns. Pure use of astringent medicines is appropriate for certain fright conditions.

Regarding accumulated dampness: When blood and fire combine with dampness, the result is fullness. Ancient formulas used decoctions adding White Peony to purify and use astringent medicines for hook-like spasms.

Fright-Wind Syndrome (Jingfeng Zheng)

In children, fright-wind disease presents as acute fright or chronic fright. The condition must be recognized carefully — acute fright, chronic fright, and slow wind in children are all serious. The three types differ from one another in their manifestations.

驚風先見之證

則面赤臉驚者虛揚恒而松氣怯神散疾迓未入去其

眼睛寬視驚必邪揚嗜而生黑風也糊則驚邪林面囟牙齕囟青

面色淡黃則面色淡白嗝不食吐則面色淡白喘息氣乏發驚左右顛亂先右後左伸手先發驚邪風入胛則面牙齕囟青

驚邪入肺則吐不食白眼目常上視乳兒之發驚左右先右後左伸手先發驚邪風入於胛則面牙齕囟青

奉神志薄不定者發驚怯情態懶不人如剝惺目面色青身黃胛反拈跌者生驚

咬牙甚久面青者發驚已有肝風也直呵視欠面色黃者身黃胛反拈跌者生驚

○直視魚目必青心○實連剁手不尋捐熱有礙直目物驚

赤視魚不必發者心○實連剁手不尋捐熱有礙直目物驚

視目亦不撮肝得發驚若有肝風藏上下左右主風動兩不上則斂兒於直目

仕不能故剁也若視就八上撮下左右主風動兩不上則斂兒不謹

動有實能轉風視連故剁也若視就入上撮下左右主風動兩不上則斂兒不謹

致搐神而生驚火相持故錢氏曰肝風心火二藏交爭而熱勝土則筋其兩皆母很驚

也動心而生驚相持故錢氏曰肝風心火二藏交爭而熱勝土木能勝土則筋其兩皆母很驚也
translation:
Early Signs Forewarning Convulsive Wind (Infantile Convulsions)

When the face is red and flushed, this is a sign of vacuity-type fright wind — the qi is timid, the spirit is scattered, and phlegm lingers without leaving.

When the eyes stare wide open, the fright is surely due to pathogenic wind rising, producing darkness and confusion; this indicates fright-pathogen entering.

When the facial color is pale yellow, or the facial color is pale white, with hiccupping, inability to eat, and vomiting, or when the face is pale white with panting and shortness of breath — convulsions will break out, with the limbs thrashing left and right, first right then left, with the hands reaching out first; this indicates pathogenic wind entering the scapular region, causing the face to clench the teeth and the fontanelle to turn blue-green.

When pathogenic fright enters the lungs, there is vomiting, inability to eat, the whites of the eyes constantly turn upward, and in nursing infants convulsions occur thrashing left and right, first right then left — this indicates pathogenic wind entering the scapular area, causing clenched teeth and a blue-green fontanelle.

When the spirit and will are thin and unsettled, fright will occur; the temperament becomes lazy and withdrawn, the eyes are dull, the face turns blue-green, the body turns yellow, and the trunk arches backward — these are signs that convulsions will arise.

When the teeth grind for a long time and the face is blue-green, convulsions have already occurred and liver wind is present. Yawning repeatedly with yellow facial color also signals impending convulsions.

When there is fixed staring with fish-like eyes and the complexion is blue-green, the condition involves the heart. When the child continuously chops the hands and cannot be controlled, with persistent heat and obstruction, this portends severe convulsions.

When the liver fails to function and the eyes stare fixedly, if liver wind is present it will surge up and down, left and right, driving the wind movement; when it cannot ascend, the child becomes unresponsive.

When heat prevails over the earth phase (Spleen), sinews are affected. As Qian Yi (錢氏) stated: liver wind and heart fire — these two viscera struggle against each other; when heat overcomes the earth phase and wood overwhelms earth, then the sinews of both are affected, and the mother viscus becomes very agitated, resulting in convulsions.

text:
驚有四證八候

急而四證生者。驚風盛發熱也。搖小兒熱盛關生疾。其師一作。八候者。其風土先發搐。慢相。八候者。擔頭者直偏兩。若寬引者。五重者。七先風。搐引者。擔目。開寬者。搐直相。八候。以引擊六七重者。引者五。反搐者。攥開者。大手。

熱而二八。發擊四驚四證相。其鷺心。發四五顏肝。台反擊六七重者。引者五。反搐者。三縮十四向後直者。引一者。若寬開擊頓目者。擔頭直偏兩者。以搦攥看者。縮目以。

手擔搦擔三指十怒視正反晴者。不向後活值。又云脊者。一引擔開擔者。若引寬相八候。顧也。生疾。

不视二三搐指擔十怒不正反晴者。已不反首。四手女擧看子。大。

二搐三擔指指怒不正反晴向後不活值。又引擔開者時者。以搦看縮目以偏。

搦三二指指怒正反晴者。又云脊已反首。四顛反者或張手或子看手之六成。

脚三或擊或肩身體四擊顛動連順在不五跳裏已反起首。四顛反反者看子上曲反者為張或顛。上曲反者或顛高右眼子六成。

直引左者由曲以為手順有如順逆反弓視通為女逆為右視反視女盡之視者看八寬之視惱者高右眼子上曲反者顛。

男子男子另料上目為我視為左順下為順寬為反弓視通為石通為左七寸右直為眼子上曲六成高右視惱者。

驚風大抵熱論虛實證別逆順治有後先

驚喉驚本無驚屬陰用藥以熱虛使然爾可以陰陽無別。以熱者以溫。慢驚以驚屬熱為陽慢急慢急驚慢為之視惱者。

驚以寒驚慢無驚屬陰用藥以熱者以溫。虛使然爾。可以陰陽無別。
translation:
Fright (Jing) Has Four Patterns and Eight Signs

The four patterns that arise in acute cases: wind-fright with vigorous heat occurring, shaking the child — vigorous heat is related to the generation of phlegm. The eight signs are: first, wind develops with twitching; then there is the slow pattern. Among the eight signs: the head tilts and turns to one side; the neck stiffens; the eyes deviate; the body arches; limbs contract and extend; the mouth opens and closes; the fists clench; and the back arches.

When heat is present, the four patterns of fright present with signs involving the heart, liver, and other organs, and the eight signs manifest in sequence with twitching, stiffening, and deviation of the eyes and head.

The hands grip and the fingers splay outward; the eyes stare upward and deviate; the body bends backward and becomes rigid; spinal arching occurs; the head turns and the jaws clench.

Regarding the deviation of gaze — in boys the eye turns to the right, in girls to the left; the body bends and arches backward; the limbs jerk and thrash.

On the general principles of treating fright-wind: distinguishing deficiency from excess, and determining correct versus contrary treatment sequences.

For throat-fright and slow-fright: these are inherently without [excess] — they belong to yin, so medicinals must be warming. In slow-fright, because the condition belongs to yin and the heat is mild, one must distinguish yin from yang carefully and apply warming treatment appropriately. Do not confuse yin and yang or treat them interchangeably.

For cold-type fright and slow-fright: these belong to yin and medication should be warming in nature, using gentle heat. One must carefully distinguish yin from yang and not conflate them.

在早晨寅時治肝瀉肝青龍湯○因肝旺熱也當搐在腎己午未時者地

黃元治肝補腎時者

角弓反張者醒為此吐者為坐諸不同頭也日仰視者為天驚吊搐

什地作聲者反張者醒為吐者為坐各不同也
translation:
It is said that in the discourse on heat, deficiency and excess conditions are as follows: In male convulsions, the eyes turn upward and are wide above; in female convulsions, the eyes turn downward and are wide below. In left-sided convulsions, the gaze turns left; in right-sided convulsions, the gaze turns right. In male convulsions, the left thumb protrudes outward; in female convulsions, the right thumb protrudes outward. Male convulsions follow the normal direction; female convulsions go against it, like a bow bent in tension, with the body arched and rigid.

When the condition enters inward, convulsions that follow the normal direction indicate an interior pattern; when they emerge outward without sound, going against the flow, then left and right connect, curving inward — this is the basis of the above distinctions regarding eye positions and thumb positions in male and female convulsions.

When heat is exuberant and wind is generated from within, treating the illness requires first addressing the onset of heron-crane (lùsī) syndrome. When this condition is at its height, wind-generated flower-pattern convulsions (huā) are difficult to treat. The heron-crane syndrome manifests with flower-patterned markings, and the pulling bow-shape shows bilateral stiffening and rigidity.

The five types of fright convulsions (jīng chù) are as follows:

1. Fright convulsions of great force — the first type. These are urgent and occur in the morning and evening, affecting both the exterior and interior, and are slow in resolution.

Those occurring in early morning at the hour of Yin (3–5 a.m.) are treated by draining the liver; the Azure Dragon Decoction is used. This is because liver excess generates heat, causing convulsions. For those occurring at the hours of Si, Wu, and Wei (9 a.m.–3 p.m.), Dihuang (Rehmannia) Pills are used to treat the liver and supplement the kidneys.

Opisthotonos (arching of the back like a bow) — the patient, when roused, vomits; various presentations differ. Upward gaze is called "heaven fright suspension convulsion."

Those who make sounds and show opisthotonos, upon arousal, vomit; each presentation differs.

散黃于涼散治驚者此亦赤肝用強肝事而後補脾時也高補因脾朝熱心散發補脾益

老傷風口中盖出氣血治未嘗發之實不可勝住者乃內生驚二次必死假者以假

translation:
Distinguishing the Severity of Convulsions and Spasms

When the Heart [fire] is dominant, one should tonify the Liver and treat the Heart; to tonify the Liver, use Dihuang Wan (Rehmannia Pill); to treat the Heart, use Daochi San (Guide Out the Red Powder). These are therefore the primary treatments.

[When treating] the Lung channel in the Tiger month (寅), tonify [accordingly].

The principle of [medical] affairs: when the Liver is dominant and prosperous, one should tonify [accordingly]; the method of tonification should supplement because the Liver, during the morning heat, with wood overacting on the Liver, drain with Qinggan (Clear the Liver) [formula], therefore [treat].

When the Heart is dominant at its [peak] time, use the scatter-red approach for the Liver; when this flourishing affects the Spleen, the disease is dominant and prosperous; one should strongly tonify the Liver, and the method should supplement, because the Spleen during morning heat, the Heart disperses, [one should] supplement the Spleen and benefit [the patient].

[When] draining the Heart, at the time [when] the Liver is affected thus — the back and its strengthening — the Liver is dominant and prosperous; after strongly supplementing, tonify the Spleen; because the Spleen during morning heat, drain the Liver's wood with the Clear [formula] to treat.

Scatter and cool to treat fright — these cases show redness of the Liver; use the method of strengthening the Liver; after this, supplement the Spleen.

[In cases of] wind-stroke with open mouth: the qi and blood come out; treatment has not yet been established; convulsions arise from within; in true cases [the patient] cannot overcome [the illness]; in false cases, life arises from within — those with false [convulsions] who wish to know whether they are false, if false they die.

In multiple cases of spasm: the exterior has symptoms of grasping and convulsion, with the body arching backward, the limbs stretching and contracting, the person immediately improving after dispersal — this is called [a mild condition]; but if the mouth is tightly closed [it is serious]; false spasms — if one wishes to know whether they are false.

[In cases where] the hands and feet are drawn together, stretching and contracting, the person immediately improves after dispersal — this is [favorable]; but if the mouth is open and there is no blue-green [discoloration], these are internal cases of double true [convulsions], not internally double.

This is treated easily in women; this type of illness [resolves with] difference. Acute infantile [convulsions]: similar to another [pattern]. Left-sided convulsions — see the section on convulsions and spasms.

Only left-sided convulsions — this is commonly named difficult-to-treat illness. Acute infantile [convulsions] in the elderly: similar to another [pattern]. Left-sided convulsions — see the convulsions and spasms section.

Convulsions and spasms arise; the hair [stands on end] — this is the mild [form] of convulsions. Convulsions and spasms then have an acute form and a chronic form; the more severe form involves shoulder movement and convulsions.

translation:
Convulsions with Sound and without Sound

When there is sound upon striking, the sound resonates with the striking. When there is sound during a woman's convulsive episode, and when a man has convulsions — looking to the right without sound, looking to the left without sound, there may be sound when looking right, relating to the opposing condition.

In men and women, the relationship pertains to Metal and Wood. Therefore, when a man looks right and then left, Metal and Wood are involved; looking in reverse to the left, with sound; looking left to Metal position, Wood position, also to Water position, relating to the knees.

Metal spreading through this, from the left, originally corresponding in view — this is the Lung, and the sound is Yang-Wood originally arising from the Lung, treating it, looking left, not complete.

The physician says: Metal spreads through this; what is called convulsive trembling and shaking then says: by this method, achieving calm, not dangerous, urgently apply this formula.

When treating, the cover is a small Wind, and at that time the disease is acute fright — urgently apply this formula.

After being able to manage the teacher — without eyes above, not tolerating it — small children when experiencing convulsive wind, going through and placing into the joints.

Therefore the heart cries out forcefully, then contrary, falsely now women store and release, corresponding daily — the small child, what is called convulsive trembling and shaking, the physician says Metal spreads — by this method achieving calm, not dangerous, urgent formula.

During convulsions, from early morning, supporting and holding upright — cannot forcibly arch the chest and grab; covering small children's fright — when convulsing, achieve calm, use the acute fright formula, urgently apply.

Bamboo, grasping hands and feet from early morning, support upright — cannot arch the chest and grab; covering small wind children's disease, especially fright, flowing and entering the joints.

One's momentum extremely stops, not reaching, injuring the child's body — above not tolerating — sending the small child, when experiencing convulsive wind, passing through and placing into joints.

translation:
When a child develops wind (convulsions), it is often triggered by fright, manifesting as prolonged convulsions and spasms throughout the body; the breath from both the body and mouth is hot, and the heart is affected.

When wind onset occurs and the convulsions stabilize, or when fright arises and then ceases, one should promptly administer medicine to purge phlegm-heat downward from the liver.

Whether due to wind or fright, if the sinews become tense and then the fright subsides, one should observe whether heat remains in the heart area.

Cool-fright type reaches the original large acupoint on the pivot; coins (acupuncture tools) address the liver. Urgently, the primary treatment for fright is to open the closed heart and calm the will.

Frequent reversal and outpouring from the middle with heat generating flushed red-purple cheeks; in robust patients this causes the large and small pathways to open, giving rise to tension or spasm.

Numerous symptoms include flushing, diarrhea, internal heat, steaming of the cheeks to a red-crimson color; the large evil fire in the two heart chambers fails to store wind; the blood and qi accumulate in disorder, and the pathogenic qi builds up in excess.

Pestilential evil is cut off, disease cannot pass through; one hundred convulsions arise with the pulse externally showing red-crimson, fire raging, contention between the two pulses, with accumulation and excess.

For the heart: use Zhenfeng Ding'yong pills nine times; treat the closed fire in the two cavities; clear the wind, blood, and qi of accumulated disorder.

In general, for wind-deficiency type the manifestation and syndrome may not be clearly of the yin type; if the syndrome shows heat, then the body becomes warm; this is called the cool type; the yang type includes restlessness.

For minor fright with major convulsions, or original convulsions which are yin-type: urgent yang-type convulsions, once stabilized, should prevent wind; the condition arises from internal warmth surging upward, or from wind arising out of heat-fright.

For the spirit and heart-stomach with exuberant heat, it is appropriate to use Baolong Pills nine times to calm and stabilize the spirit; for young children, use Jinfeng pills; for the ling-type, use Zhen pills to suppress convulsions.

For the heart, use Zhenfeng Ding'yong Pills nine times; disperse and preserve, then urgently open and harmonize wind and stomach; stabilize and suppress convulsions from the heart outward.

Pestilential evil is cut off so disease cannot pass; one hundred convulsions arise, with the pulse externally showing red-crimson and fire raging in great contention.

When onset occurs and convulsions stabilize, or fright arises and then subsides, one should promptly use medicine to purge phlegm-heat downward and calm the heart.

translation:
Slow (Chronic) Fright-Wind (Mànjīngfēng)

Slow fright-wind occurs after recovery from a serious illness, or following vomiting and diarrhea, or after excessive consumption of cold medicines. Symptoms include: facial color of bluish-yellow or pale white, upward rolling of the eyes, exposed eyeballs, slow convulsions with delayed responses. Use White Atractylodes and Aquilaria Powder. When the condition has been long-standing and treatment has failed, due to wind excess, the stool turns greenish-white; this is slow fright-wind arising spontaneously. In boys, when wind is excessive, the stool is greenish-white; this is slow fright-wind. In cases where the middle abdomen is deficient and cold, add to the formula anti-wind herbs; if the abdomen is distended with deficiency-cold, the stools are greenish-white, indicating slow fright-wind of long standing.

Add Saposhnikovia (Fangfeng) and bile. When the liver is severely deficient, the limbs and mouth frequently exhibit trembling, the eyes roll upward, the face shows yellow streaks, and the channels are affected; if the patient is female, the signs of fright are severe, the eyes stare upward, or the head sways — this is slow fright-wind of urgency.

When there is vomiting at intervals, or sacred [medicines] are used without producing fright, the eyes may stare, the head may sway; these are signs of slow fright. The eyes, mouth, hands and feet are half-open, indicating slow fright of urgency. Use Yin-nourishing, heat-reducing formulas; if vomiting or phlegm occurs, do not force feeding.

For the large formula: add medicines to strengthen the stomach, transmitting the slow fright formula with Atractylodes and Borneol, combined with resuscitating Yang-dispersing powder. If phlegm is present, use multiple doses appropriately.

Use Wind-Dispersing and Stomach-Regulating Yellow Aconite with Cicada Shell Powder, combined with Yang-awakening powder; if there is no water return, use wind-calming methods cautiously with aconite.

Use sulphur combined with aconite for abdominal weakness; use Sedating-Fright Family Powder with Croton; be cautious and refrain from all [inappropriate] methods.

When there is slippery diarrhea that will not stop, guard against slow fright-wind. If greenish stools persist, this indicates fright mixed with wind; even if improved, one must be extremely careful and grounded in treatment.

Towangseon (Supplementing Earth Formula - Primary Source)
Supplement Earth as treasure, origin of Earth, after which Earth governs transformation. For vomiting from deficiency of the middle, great wind, wonderful effect of licorice, slow fright wind, five divisions, great region, water-earth diarrhea, middle diarrhea - for this wood and fire.

Hwangsi-tang (Huangshi Decoction)
Dose: several qian. Treats slow fright wind. For five days when spirit is vigorous, the method must include aconite (fuzi), fresh arisaema soaked, each one qian. Grind into powder, make paste with flour, form into pills.

Onbaek-gu (Warm White Pills)
Seven-to-nine pills up to large. Three doses of rice decoction, five qian, whole scorpion, stir-fried white [ingredient], one qian. Grind into powder, make paste with flour, form into pills.

Gamimi Mokbu-tang (Modified Aconite and Atractylodes Decoction)
Each dose: white atractylodes 2 qian, licorice, Polygonum multiflorum, for vomiting and diarrhea that does not stop, gastrodia, for slow fright wind, ginseng, white atractylodes, aromatics, licorice each 5 fen. Two qian aconite (fuzi), fresh arisaema soaked, each one liang, nutmeg two pieces. For vomiting and diarrhea with cold in the organs causing persistent diarrhea.

Seonbja-san (Awakening the Spine Powder)
One fen, whole scorpion two fen. Decoct in water, take one full dose. Each two qian, ginger, licorice, costus root, each five fen. Can be taken as a single dose.

Nursing Milk Formula (Niang Ru Fang)

Take perilla (Zisu) to treat slow-type fright (man jing). Ingredients: Ginseng 1 qian, Huoxiang (agastache) 5 fen, Chenxiang (agarwood), Chenpi (tangerine peel), Shenqu (medicated leaven), Maiya (malt) — each 1 qian for treating slow fright, Zhike (bitter orange). Do not exceed the prescribed amount.

Take and administer immediately. This is an appropriate and effective method. Suppress and administer as directed. Now when the child recovers, after several days: Fuzi (aconite) 2 pieces, Baihua (white flower), Quzhi (maggot) half, add Chuanwu (aconite root), Nanfang (southern wind herb) 1 part.

1 fen. Treats slow-onset conditions. Processed Banxia (pinellia), deficiency-type slow wind. Tiannanzixing (heavenly star), Baisui (hundred years), Wuliang (limitless), two Fuzi (aconite), Baihua (white flowers), Quzhi half, add Chuanwu, Nan — 1 fen.

Decoct and take. Treats slow fright. Whole scorpion, pure yin syndrome, with scorpion 2, Junzi Tang (decoction), Chanchu (toad) 2, add water.

Toad-Scorpion Powder (Chan Xie San)
2, slow fright wind. 21 pieces, ginger 3 slices, Nanxing (Arisaema) still 1, it is appropriate to use this medicine: whole scorpion 7, toad powder, each dose taken at retreat.

Miraculous Efficacy Powder (Shen Xiao San)
1 qian, treats water-related [conditions]. 8, slow fright. 3, 1 slice, Nanxing 2 fen half. Right [side ingredients]: sparrow powder, each dose.

Two [doses of] arsenic for slow fright with bleeding. The three ingredients are all ground to powder; separately use from the left hand of a male: clove 1 piece, toad 1 zi (small measure), spread [apply].

Burn medicine powder, rub on child's lips. Use right middle finger to apply. Ingredients: ginger powder, coptis, ginseng, one portion of wood fragrance, white lotus seed, cardamom, licorice, each one fen, for the four limbs.

Three-Ingredient Tianjiangzi Powder:

Treats chronic fright wind. Soybean three fen, pinellia, white peony, each dry-fried, with coptis, ginseng, by the qian.

Life-Protecting Pill:
Angelica root, Sichuan lovage, each lightly fried, various wind [ingredients], two zhu fen. Dry ginger, blast-roasted, one portion, fermented grain flour, fried, aconite, roasted, fragrant white grains, one fen, stir-fried silkworm. [Taken] with peppermint decoction.

Dry-fried, blast-roasted ginger, cow bezoar, roasted, fragrant white grain, one qian, fried whole [scorpion].

Two qian, half fen, spirit fragrance six fen, scorpion tail seven pieces, cow bezoar, chlorite schist, pearl, three pieces each.

Serving with Qingzhou Baiyuan pills: take frequently. The formula's verified efficacy, though the person is elderly, awaits the nature of intake. Jinye Dan: for children with diarrhea, to transform and resolve seizures, revive and save many. Adjust with eight qian.

Verified Treatments for Fright Wind (Jingfeng):
Gualou (trichosanthes) and other medicines are observed for the child's vomiting and diarrhea. Various medicines are used for the seizures until the body transforms into epilepsy. The condition reaches the diaphragm. Large and small stools cannot pass; the child cannot open its eyes. When regulated and cleared, if the child cannot eat and dies, the deficiency causes the fetal qi to be large and the stool small. The child cannot urinate or defecate. The fetus is full and the body becomes stout. When closed eyes are observed, treat with nine [doses]. The bitterness of the formula hinders. When the stool is large and the urine flows, recovery follows with ten qian administered to save many.

Signs of Intractable Slow Fright Wind (Man Jingfeng):
The head shakes, the eyes stare without turning, speech is delayed and slow, there is a moaning sound, the pulse at the head is exposed, the mouth cannot open or close, the hands and feet lose prohibition. The four limbs are sluggish. The spirit is lost. The eyes are half-open and glazed. The skin is exposed. The eyelids droop slowly. Pain appears in the limbs. The mouth and face show sores. The spirit is as if removed.

Medicines used: Six flavors of Dihuang (Rehmannia), slow-acting for painful fright, four limbs alone with sounds showing symptoms, the sound is like the kidneys' [deterioration], hence after this comes ulceration.

translation:
Slow Spleen Wind (Chronic Spleen Wind)

The treatment of Slow Spleen Wind arises after chronic fright, vomiting, and diarrhea. If the spleen disease has been transmitted to its extreme, this is what is called "chronic deficiency wind-heat," which is difficult to treat. The key point is what is called fright deficiency: observe carefully, for this is the most critical matter. When the eyes close and the spirit becomes confused, this is the stage of chronic illness which is extremely difficult to treat and incomparable in severity.

When the eyes show signs, and the spirit is depleted without the spleen being replenished, one can receive qi [only with great difficulty]. In the interval of chronic heat therapy, the essentials must be observed.

The eyes show signs of heat, fanning heaviness, making it difficult to open them fully; the eyes are heavy, half-closed, and the four limbs show wind symptoms with openings and outward signs. Chronic cases require careful observation as the most important matter.

When [the condition] transmits inward to the organs, it moves quickly, and already the qi has spread to the left and right of the forehead; the eyes are half-open, half-closed, pressing downward in the lower yin, advancing to the eighth intestine entering the chest, manifesting on the face and at the mouth.

In speech, the chronic transmission of wind enters the organs rapidly; chronic fright qi already [affects] the neck and face; the eyes and bladder turn greenish; there is foul smell at the mouth and tongue; one should predict that the head and hands will drop low, and the pulse will become sunken.

When the eyes close partially due to wind, it is called inability to open and manage [things], and confusion sets in. In chronic cases, the head and neck show wind symptoms, the eyes and [urinary] system turn greenish, there is foul smell at the mouth; one should predict the head drooping, hands lowering, and the pulse becoming sunken and slow.

Slight deficiency of yin qi, [qi] attaches at the extreme, unable to contain [itself] or the body, extreme [condition] at ten or more [stages], the body temperature covers the four limbs, the chronic pulse is sunken.

All [such cases are] transmitted: use warming and tonifying methods, chronic black chest, use medicinal governance, again unable to grow, attach [medicine] to the second and fourth [stages], and the chronic fright with attached wind pulse will become sunken.

Grind [the medicines] in oil, transmit them, and take with thin congee soup, one qian of liquid pill with ginger, this is the Ginger Wind Return Yang formula (Huiyang Yuanzi). If [the patient is] like a half-wilted plant, use [the formula] without dispersing.

For small infants with facial pallor, though mature, taking medicines such as [pearl or green formulas], diarrhea will cease and the extremities will recover. Though the head and abdomen may be hot or distended, [recovery is possible].

translation:
Gan Disease (Nutritional Deficiency Disorders in Children)

"Gan" means wasting: it refers to emaciation and deficiency of blood and qi. In children up to the age of twenty, conditions include: Gan exhaustion, spinal Gan, milk Gan, Gan with organ exposure, and organ Gan. There is also Ding-xi (infantile malnutrition), milk Gan, exposed-organ Gan. Various formulas exist for treating each type of Gan disease, including Crow-milk swelling.

Distension Gan — among the ten types of Gan: In the dry type, there is loss of breath, the hair and skin are abnormal, and it is attributed to insufficiency of sweetness reaching the viscera; accumulation and stagnation develop, and upon diagnosis many types of organ Gan appear, including Crow-head, milky eyes, white of the eye, self-perspiration, acid diarrhea, oral ulceration, foul smell, white coating.

In the skin-Gan type: the nose is distended, the intestines knot, the body contracts, the stomach and intestines are congested, the nasal passages are blocked, the mouth is pale and thick; therefore many organ Gan presentations appear.

Acid and salty foods damage the belly; the back resembles a bird's spine; the patient drinks excessively of water; in the mornings women with heat present likewise; the body experiences dryness and thirst, the teeth become loose, diarrhea occurs, the eyes become white.

Kidney-Gan: charcoal-like, the pain does not recover, drying is severe; the intestines of organ Gan should be urgently treated; initially the mouth emits a foul odor, acid diarrhea, oral sores.

Complete stagnation: the teeth blacken, trembling occurs, the blood is lost; using dry and firm methods for the teeth and intestines; the condition is urgent and requires treatment; some relief may be obtained.

Ai-Gan (affection Gan) and Milk-Gan: both expose the earth-Gan; it becomes critical and fatal; scorched heat is severe; the organs dry out; the viscera have no disease but the toxin and dampness combine. Gan with swelling and distension.

Gan-gate: heat accumulates; the patient crosses between cold and heat, alternating; originally the viscera become diseased together with the toxin; Ding type.

Treatment: the stool is white in color, urination is difficult and resembles rice-wash water; this gives rise to the name "organ disease," also called "Gan-fat."

Deficiency-heat conditions: for all Gan conditions, based on the root organ, supplement according to the need — for example, if afternoon tidal fever develops and then subsides, this pertains to the Heart.

translation:
Mugogo-gam (Infantile Malnutrition Disorder — Mugogo type)

The signs of Mugogo-gam are: the face turns yellow, the hair grows straight and stiff, there are periodic bouts of high fever, and the child cannot eat or drink. Over the course of days and months the child becomes progressively more yellow and emaciated, approaching death. During the episodes of high fever, it is said that a bird called the "Mugogo bird" flies overhead during the day, and its feathers and down pollute the child's household. When washing the child's clothes, one should air-dry them outdoors in the daylight. If there is phlegm, or if a rash-like residue appears, once it breaks open and is pressed, it initially feels soft; over time it grows longer. The child's vital energy becomes diffuse and scattered throughout the body, invading the flesh and muscles.

The flesh of the hands and feet wastes away, and the abdomen becomes distended and hard.

Tukgok-gam (Sobbing/Crying Malnutrition Disorder)

[Regarding treatment:] Charcoal and similar materials should generally be used in sequence. The layers come and go, forming shapes resembling medicinal pills, distributed in cloth bags. [Various preparations] are produced; the formula reverses the Mugogo pathology. It addresses spleen-stomach distress and thirst, relieving the deficiency within the bones.

[Further signs:] In the eighth month, around the ninth [day], the neck and abdomen show symptoms; the yellow color gradually spreads, and the pills for [treating] the condition link together through the abdomen and limbs, where the tissue rots.

Jeong-gok-gam (Wailing Malnutrition Disorder)

Pollo-gam (Exposure-Depletion Malnutrition Disorder)

This condition is difficult to treat. Daily it progresses; the body deteriorates. It should be treated with the cloth-bag pill formula of various Mugogo categories, addressing spleen and stomach weakness.

Gam-gal-gam (Thirst-Malnutrition Disorder)

Difficult to treat. There is night-time irritability with constant desire to drink; chronic coughing; aversion to milk and food; hardness like stone; the complexion becomes like [wood].

Gam-no-gam (Taxation-Malnutrition Disorder)

[Treat with] silver-ash formula. Can be treated. It is appropriate to use the chronic-cough pill, with additions, to transform the condition and bring recovery.

The Fei Er Wan treats accumulation masses (pi ji) and hardened cakes (bing) as the main [condition]; this medicine disperses gan (infantile malnutrition) and dissolves accumulation. Ingredients: dry-fried medicated leaven (shen qu), dry-fried coptis (huang lian), [Jade formula ingredients]:

[Processing instructions involving] chen pi (aged tangerine peel) to harmonize the stomach, stop diarrhea, stabilize the intestines, reduce heat, coptis (huang lian), each 5 [qian].

Shi Wei Lu Hui Wan (Ten-Ingredient Aloe Pill)
[This formula of] ten pills treats gan accumulation masses and kills parasites. Ingredients include: [various aromatics], wu yi (elm cake), harmonized with aromatics, green [herb], [phoenix/bird ingredient], to drive out heat; hu huang lian (Picrorhiza), lei wan (thunder ball fungus).

translation:
[These entries describe types of fever (熱) in children's medicine, categorized by location and nature:]

General: Fevers include wind-heat, cold-heat, strong heat, deficiency heat. The location of heat on the face indicates which organ is affected: the left cheek indicates Liver Heat, the right cheek indicates Lung Heat, the forehead indicates Heart Heat, the nose indicates Spleen Heat, and the chin indicates Kidney Heat. Generalized body heat indicates deficiency heat. For children's febrile diseases, preparations using water can disperse heat to the exterior — this is an excellent remedy. If the child wishes to drink water, it is due to heat; do not use warm tonifying medicines. See the Stone Powder entry for further reference.

Liver Heat: In Liver Heat, the hands and feet are red and hot. The child pulls at clothing. Use the Clear Heart Pill (清心丸). See the relevant entry.

Heart Heat: In Heart Heat, the face and complexion are red, and there is heat in the mouth. Use Dragon-based formulas. See the eye-related entries.

Spleen Heat: In Spleen Heat, the face is red, there is heat rising with thirst. Use the appropriate dispersing formulas.

Lung Heat: In Lung Heat, the right cheek is red; there may also be redness in the nose, and a yellowish-white complexion. Use cold-dispersing formulas.

Kidney Heat: In Kidney Heat, the complexion tends to be dark with a yellowish hue. Symptoms appear at fixed times, with recurrent episodes. Bowel irregularities may be present.

Tidal Heat (Cyclical Fever): Tidal fever occurs in recurring waves. Address the underlying pattern; symptoms such as dry mouth and constipation may accompany it.

Fetal Heat (Congenital Heat): In fetal heat, the infant appears red and yellow, refuses to nurse. It is appropriate to use Rehmannia Decoction (生地黃湯) and eye-wash formulas as indicated.

translation:
Bone-steaming fever (骨蒸熱):
For bone-steaming fever, it is appropriate to use Digu Pi San (Lycium Root Bark Powder) for night sweats. [Section] five.

Phlegm-heat (痰熱):
Phlegm-heat with heart vexation and agitation; symptoms include generalized heat, red face, dry mouth, and tidal fever. [Use] Yi formula.

Malarial fever (瘧熱):
Malarial fever with alternating chills and heat; it is appropriate to use Li Jiu (Pear Decoction) for cough and blockage in the diaphragm causing difficulty.

Wind-cold fever (風寒熱):
Disordered fever with yawning and heat; appropriate when there is generalized heat and qi rising from the mouth.

High fever (壯熱):
For those with convulsions and high fever, when the whole body is hot and the patient drinks water — whether adult or child — if symptoms are unresolved and have not dispersed, and are severe.

Excess heat (實熱):
For nourishing and clearing; appropriate for those with generalized fever, thirst with desire to drink water; for both adults and children with difficult urination and constipation.

Deficiency heat (虛熱):
For those with deficiency heat, it is appropriate to administer bone-nourishing decoctions with various herbs.

Cold Water Stone Powder (寒水石散):
For various fevers in children, promotes urination, clears heart heat, and expels convulsive phlegm. Cold water stone [is the main ingredient].

[Formulas for] cold months, summer heat, warm and hot conditions: mix with water and take down. Ingredients: Gypsum (石膏), Curcuma (鬱金), Mint (薄荷), Licorice (甘草), equal portions.

Ganlu Drink (甘露飲): grind equal portions into powder — Gypsum, Curcuma, Mint, Licorice.

Thirty-one liang and a half; grind the right [ingredients] into powder. One qian of [herb], adjusted with mint, to be swallowed.

Accumulation and Masses (Ji Pi)
[Discussion:] Milk accumulation, food accumulation, fat accumulation, gan accumulation — these arise from food stagnation. When a child's abdomen is distended with accumulation, the body becomes thin and weak, the belly bloats, gan syndrome develops, the face turns yellow, the intestines and abdomen rumble, and the person sleeps a great deal — these are signs of accumulation.

Food accumulation transforms into gan accumulation when food stagnates and the body becomes emaciated, the belly swells without normal tone, heat arises, the face is sallow, there is abdominal distension and intestinal rumbling — this constitutes the syndrome of accumulation.

[Treatment:] peppermint, lamp-rush [rush pith], pig heart, ophiopogon, [made into a] decoction or large dose of three qian. Grind into powder, wrap [in paper], each dose one pill taken as before.

Jimsik-gu (Pill to Promote Food Intake)

Ingredients: Three dan (units) of rice, large malt, two portions of Smilax (Baksu/Biho), cooked barley, one qian of Gleditsia seeds (Jobokryang/豬牙皂), Crataegus (Sanzha), five fen of Angelica root (Danggwi), one substitute of cinnabar (Zhusha), mixed each three qian, ground fine and made into pills.

Siksik-gu (Pill to Digest Food)

Ingredients: Fermented wheat leaven (Sinkok/神麴), dried tangerine peel (Chinpi/陳皮), mixed together. Also called Soyu-gu (消乳九). Contains: Sinkok (神麴), malt (麥芽), each roasted, half a stone weight, ground fine.

[Clinical commentary]
When a child does not stop drinking and the food stagnates, forming accumulations of milk and food, and the intestinal pathogen persists, the food accumulations interlock. If the lumps do not resolve, one should use [the pill] to clear and transform the stomach and nourish the spleen. Shen Liu-qi [a physician] treats this with Sinkok and Cheonggeum (千金) formulas.

[On the condition of milk accumulation/fat child syndrome]
When a child suffers from milk food illness, with pain lying hidden in the abdomen — the Fat Child Pill (Biasik-gu/肥兒九) is indicated. If there is a hard lump (pi/癖), the child cannot eat properly; the lump forms in the stomach, causing fever, loosening of the teeth, and ultimately develops into the abdominal Fat Child condition. When there is pathogenic water distension below with tidal [fever], the method should gradually resolve it — use the Fat Child Pill.

Remove the skin and membrane from [the ingredients]; white aconite accessory root, with southern star [Arisaema], [process until] no longer raw; [take] one coin-weight each; dissolve in milk. This is the main formula: smooth [texture], two parts ground mineral [light powder/calomel].
Using milk, white scallion, prepare cake, boil, three cups, one portion per year of age. Grind evenly, mix into a paste, ten to fourteen pills.

For turbid [conditions] arising from heat; use Sanleng (Three-edged bulrush rhizome) with southern star [Arisaema] to disperse accumulations; chew and eat. For children with spleen accumulation: combine atractylodes and others with Sanleng, stir-fry together; tangerine peel, each equal part.
Blast-fry [ingredients]; medicated leaven and malt, stir-fry together; grind into powder. For children, this formula — also known as White Cake — is used for the many types of accumulation disorders.

Prepare as a decoction powder. Use white flour, make into a gruel with water. Mix nine times steamed, bean-sized pills. Each ingredient two qian, mixed together, half portion. [Various ingredients processed by stir-frying, grinding, etc.]

Mix together, nine portions, one qian each. Treat abdominal accumulation and masses. Use the medicine, ground to powder. Make into pills the size of a date pit. Each five qian. Badou (croton seed), three fen. Rougui (cinnamon), one qian. The remainder dissolves the pus.

Qingwei Yangpi Tang (Stomach-Clearing Spleen-Nourishing Decoction)
For children. One qian. Chenpi (aged tangerine peel). Baishu (white atractylodes). Tuchifu (red poria with earth). Gancao (licorice). Shu (processed). Fry until done. Each ingredient one qian. Apply the above as a decoction.

translation:
Remedies for Vomiting and Diarrhea

Aromatic Water: 2 fen. Slice the ingredients coarsely; for each dose use 3 qian, with one and a half cups of water, decoct down to one cup, remove the dregs, and take warm.

Vomiting and Diarrhea

First: When an infant suffers from vomiting and diarrhea, one should promptly use Qingtu (Cleared Earth) preparation, combined with Hewei Pill (Stomach-Harmonizing Pill) and milk feeding; taking it will immediately stop the vomiting and diarrhea. This is called the Golden Cake Powder.

When the cause is stagnation in the stomach leading to vacuity and heat, use Purple Pill; after taking it, if there is white diarrhea, use침沉 Decoction Powder with aromatic orange and cake powder mixed together. For initial vomiting and diarrhea in newborns, if there is milk-induced injury with turquoise-colored diarrhea, use White Powder.

For injury to the stomach causing vomiting, if there is cold vomiting, use Yisan (Benefit Powder) combined with Huanglü Powder; for infants of various ages use Xiangjiā Decoction.

For vomiting and diarrhea occurring in a particular month, with bodily accumulation of phlegm, use Benefit Powder combined with Huanglü Powder; for newborns with lockjaw (neonatal tetanus), assist and encourage feeding.

For vomiting with phlegm due to cold, use the main Benefit Powder; for newborns with lockjaw, assist and encourage.

When wind-stroke and convulsive twitching are present, with leg stiffness, use Large Green Paste (Daqing Gao); if the child frequently regurgitates and has convulsions and sinew problems, use the pill form.

For cases where the condition has lasted years, with chronic milk regurgitation, slow eye movement, and sinew problems, use the iron-burning pill.

translation:
Harmony Stomach Pill (Hwawi-gu / 和胃九)

[Dosage:] For infants of 9-19 months, use one small pill; for children under one year old who have vomiting and diarrhea, this harmonizes the stomach and promotes milk feeding — most effective. Ingredients: Mountain yam (Dioscorea), woody musk (Mu Xiang), ginseng, white atractylodes, white poria, tangerine peel, licorice — each one liang [half tael]; ginger paste to bind. [Take] as powder, one qian, mixed with honey, swallowed.

Stomach-Assisting Paste (助胃膏)

Take one qian of the powder, mix with honey and swallow.

Treats vomiting and diarrhea in infants, harmonizes the stomach and promotes milk feeding. Most effective. Ingredients: Mountain yam, woody musk — each two qian; white cardamom, white poria, tangerine peel, licorice — each two qian. Grind into powder, bind with ginger paste.

Discussion and Diagnosis of Vomiting and Diarrhea (吐瀉論證)

When a child of five years vomits and has diarrhea, if the eyes are bright and the face has color — this is normal constitution. If the eyes are white with black pupils, the face is pale, and the child does not want to eat, this relates to the liver. If there is vomiting and persistent diarrhea, the child is weak in kidney qi and the muscles are thin. If the face is black and the child does not sleep well, this indicates accumulated illness.

In women, loss of blood leads to vomiting and diarrhea. When it enters the liver, one loses appetite; when it enters the heart, there is fright; when it enters the spleen, there is diarrhea.

This method should not be used to purge blood deficiency — it is for vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, and resolving food accumulation.

If digestion is impaired and there is food accumulation, [use the appropriate remedy].

translation:
Fontanelle Conditions

Regarding the condition called "open fontanelle" (解顱): In young children, when the cranial sutures do not close and the brain remains exposed, this is called "open fontanelle." This is caused by insufficiency of kidney qi, since the kidneys govern bone. When marrow is insufficient, the brain's fontanelle remains open. Some cases occur because the child has not yet reached full development, so proper growth cannot be achieved. There will be restlessness, and in serious cases one must stimulate development. Treatment includes Tiannanxing Powder and similar formulas.

The fundamental approach is to administer the Six-Ingredient Decoction. One may also apply the Three-Yellow paste. Tiannanxing Powder or similar remedies may be added for cases where the sutures remain open.

Three Spirit Powder (三神散): Used for treating open fontanelle. Use dried ginger juice mixed with ginger, seven qian; moxibustion at the fontanelle; Tiannanxing, upper half; for small children, use red heart [ingredients]; vinegar applied externally, five qian. Directions on right.

Tiannanxing Powder (天南星散): Same as above. Use large doses; moxibustion at fontanelle; roast Tiannanxing until slightly scorched, grind to powder, effective immediately; Xixin (asarum), red-faced heart, each with vinegar applied externally, five qian. Directions on right.

Sunken Fontanelle (顱陷): Affects the spleen and fontanelle region. Apply paste to the fontanelle. Use Tiannanxing; if breastfeeding is improper or irregular, the condition worsens; if wind-cold or heat attacks, the condition worsens further.

When heat surges upward, the fontanelle becomes hard and prominent, sweating occurs, and the fontanelle rises high. This is caused by irregular nursing, or excessive wind-cold or heat.

Green moxa and yang energy draw fluids, leading to fontanelle conditions; loss of blood causes weakness and sunken pits in the fontanelle, preventing proper upward development. Fright and convulsions may also occur.

Formulas for Preventing Smallpox

The chapter on Formulas for Preventing Smallpox includes: the Method of Taking Cinnabar, the Unique Sacred Decoction, the Secret Formula for the Smallpox-Prevention Red Pill.

Method of Taking Cinnabar

Take refined cinnabar that has been water-ground to a fine powder. Mix with honey. Adjust the dose according to the child's size. Each dose is five fen, formed into three pills, taken down with honey-water. There is no restriction on timing. Those who use the dark-room method do not use this.
